memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Abram traveled through the land as far as the site of the great tree of Moreh at Shechem. At that time the Canaanites were in the land. The Lord appeared to Abram and said, "To your offspring I will give this land." So he built an altar there to the Lord, who had appeared to him. - Gen 12:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abram arrives in Canaan, and Scripture adds a pointed detail: "At that time the Canaanites were in the land." The land God promised was already full of other people. Abram owned not one inch of it. And right there, in that occupied territory, God appears and says, "To your offspring I will give this land."

The promise came when the evidence said otherwise. Abram could see Canaanites everywhere and no title deed anywhere. God's promises often arrive in circumstances that seem to contradict them - a childless couple promised descendants, an occupied land promised as an inheritance.

And what does Abram do? He builds an altar. He worships. He does not demand proof or wait for the land to clear. He responds to God's word with worship, staking his life on a promise he cannot yet see. That is faith: worshipping the Promise-Maker before you see the promise kept.

We should be careful here - this specific land promise was made to Abram and his offspring, not directly to us. But the God who made it has not changed. He is still the God who speaks promises into impossible circumstances and keeps every word. Whatever "Canaanites" fill the land of your situation today, God's word stands. Build your altar. Worship the God who keeps His promises, even when you cannot yet see how.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you waiting to see the promise before you worship the Promise-Maker?
- What circumstances seem to contradict what God has said?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Faithful God, You speak promises into impossible circumstances and keep every one. Help me worship You before I see the outcome, trusting Your word above what my eyes can see.
Amen.
